messages.content:
You are composing music in an isolated workspace. Use the bash tool to run commands and complete the task.
Each command runs in /workspace in a fresh bash shell; files and the FT2 session persist between commands. Budget: 100 steps and 30 minutes; a step is one reply, and every tool call in it runs in order.
The `ft2 list` command describes the tracker tools. `ft2 call TOOL 'JSON_OBJECT'` calls one tool. `ft2 batch FILE.json` executes a list of {"name": TOOL, "arguments": {...}} calls in order.
This FT2 build exposes samples, instruments by name, patterns, order, tempo, save and render. Envelopes and note-to-sample mapping are unavailable; shape sounds in the sample data itself.
Python 3 and NumPy are available for creating original sound material, editing files, and analyzing renders. Writing the XM bytes yourself is allowed; the module is judged as a file. Keep it a real tracker module, with instruments and patterns doing the work, not one long pre-rendered sample.
The workspace is offline: no network, no coding-agent client, no skill library. You cannot hear audio; render to WAV with module_render and inspect the result with NumPy to check your work, then revise.
A keygen tune plays in a loop. Compose so the module loops cleanly from its end back to its restart position.
Save the final editable module as /workspace/submission/tune.xm. A WAV preview and source scripts may accompany it. A trusted process renders the final XM separately.
Submit by running exactly this command:
echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
Submission ends the session. There is no second attempt or post-submission repair.

You have FastTracker II and Python/NumPy at your disposal. Make an original keygen tune. Music only.
Choose the sound, tempo, harmony, rhythm, instruments, length and arrangement yourself.

{"command":"python3 - <<'PY'
import numpy as np, base64, json, os
fs=8363
n=int(0.2*fs); t=np.arange(n)/fs
x=(0.5*np.sin(2*np.pi*261.625*t)*np.exp(-t*5))
pcm=(x*32767).astype('<i2')
b64=base64.b64encode(pcm.tobytes()).decode()
cmds=[
 {'name':'module_new','arguments':{'channels':2,'name':'test'}},
 {'name':'song_set','arguments':{'bpm':150,'speed':6,'length':1,'loop_start':0}},
 {'name':'sample_create_from_pcm','arguments':{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'pcm':b64,'encoding':'int16','name':'sine'}},
 {'name':'sample_set','arguments':{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':64,'panning':128,'relative_note':0,'flags':16}},
 {'name':'pattern_set_length','arguments':{'pattern':0,'rows':16}},
 {'name':'pattern_set_cell','arguments':{'pattern':0,'row':0,'channel':0,'note':'C-4','instrument':1,'volume':64}},
 {'name':'order_set','arguments':{'position':0,'pattern':0}},
 {'name':'module_save','arguments':{'path':'/workspace/test.xm','format':'xm'}},
 {'name':'module_render','arguments':{'path':'/workspace/test.wav','rate':44100,'bits':16,'loops':1,'amp':64}},
]
open('/workspace/test_batch.json','w').write(json.dumps(cmds))
PY
ft2 batch /workspace/test_batch.json > /workspace/test_batch.log 2>&1
cat /workspace/test_batch.log | tail -20
ls -l /workspace/test.xm /workspace/test.wav
python3 - <<'PY'
import wave, numpy as np
w=wave.open('/workspace/test.wav','rb')
print(w.getparams())
data=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2')
print(data.shape, data.max(), data.min(), np.sqrt(np.mean(data.astype(float)**2)))
PY"}

import numpy as np, base64, json, os
fs=8363
L=32
x=np.sin(2*np.pi*np.arange(L)/L)*0.6
pcm=(x*32767).astype('<i2')
b64=base64.b64encode(pcm.tobytes()).decode()
cmds=[
 {'name':'module_new','arguments':{'channels':2,'name':'loopt'}},
 {'name':'song_set','arguments':{'bpm':125,'speed':6,'length':1,'loop_start':0}},
 {'name':'sample_create_from_pcm','arguments':{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'pcm':b64,'encoding':'int16','name':'loop sine'}},
 {'name':'sample_set','arguments':{'instrument':1,'sample':0,'volume':64,'panning':128,'loop_start':0,'loop_length':L,'flags':17}},
 {'name':'pattern_set_length','arguments':{'pattern':0,'rows':16}},
 {'name':'pattern_set_cell','arguments':{'pattern':0,'row':0,'channel':0,'note':'C-4','instrument':1,'volume':64}},
 {'name':'order_set','arguments':{'position':0,'pattern':0}},
 {'name':'module_render','arguments':{'path':'/workspace/loopt.wav','rate':44100,'bits':16,'loops':1,'amp':16}},
]
open('/workspace/loopt.json','w').write(json.dumps(cmds))
PY
ft2 batch /workspace/loopt.json > /workspace/loopt.log 2>&1; tail -20 /workspace/loopt.log
python3 - <<'PY'
import wave, numpy as np
w=wave.open('/workspace/loopt.wav','rb'); data=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),dtype='<i2').reshape(-1,2)
print(w.getparams(),data.max(),data.min(),np.sqrt(np.mean(data.astype(float)**2)))
# RMS start/mid/end windows
for start in [0,10000,50000,100000]:
    d=data[start:start+5000]
    print(start, np.sqrt(np.mean(d.astype(float)**2)), d.max(), d.min())
PY"}
